correctness.rationale: The multiplication expansion v²=−(b²+c²)1+tbc(i+j) forces the three unital planes; any nonunital plane ker(a+ub+vc), with generators i−u1,j−v1, has u²=v²=−1 and uv=0, impossible over any field. det[1,x,x²]=tbc(b−c) traps all one-dimensional closed lines in those planes. The quadratic quotient types K[z]/(z²+1), K[z]/(z²−tz+2) give the exact split/double/inert line, unit, idempotent and nilpotent counts, including characteristic two. Two-sided-inverse commutator forces a non-scalar inverse into the same commutative plane; uniqueness follows. Inclusion–exclusion over planes with pairwise intersection K1 gives s_r=q^(3r)−3q^(2r)+2q^r. Independent direct multiplication and exhaustive projective-closure/unit counts match q=2,3,5,7 across seven parameters; all character cases arise. Finite checks corroborate, universal conclusion follows the algebraic proof.
